drafted_from: tools/pointillist-film/tool-rows.json (tool:render-a-pointillist-frame), examples/encode_frame_request.rs, test/pointillist-film.test.mjs; the example was run here with cargo
start_here: Say to your AI: "Render the frame at 0.5 seconds of my two-cell film from request.json into frame.pfcf." It runs encode_frame_request on your computer and tells you where the packed frame file is.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads one request file and writes one packed frame file.
instructions: 1. Install rust (cargo) and clone the Workshop repository. The first run builds the program (about a minute; a few seconds once built).

2. Write request.json from the film you want: {config: {grid, limits, style}, script: {targets, segments}, time_seconds}. Each target is a list of cells, one {color {r,g,b,a}, opacity, scale} for each grid cell; each segment says when it runs and the weight of each target as small expressions over time.

3. The AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: "tool:render-a-pointillist-frame"} and runs: cargo run --release --quiet --manifest-path trillion-workshop/tools/pointillist-film/Cargo.toml --target-dir /tmp/pointillist-film-build --example encode_frame_request -- request.json frame.pfcf

4. Nothing prints on success: the answer is frame.pfcf, which begins PFCF. The same request always gives the same bytes. A request that breaks a limit or names a missing target prints the reason on standard error, exits non-zero and writes no file.

worked_examples.title: One frame of a two-cell film at half a second
worked_examples.ask: Render the frame at 0.5 seconds of my two-cell film.
worked_examples.given: From tools/pointillist-film/test/pointillist-film.test.mjs (the one-frame test) and run here with cargo: request.json is a two-cell film (grid 2 columns by 1 row, gap 0.1; limits max 8 columns, 8 rows, 64 cells, 4 targets, 4096 frame bytes; style opacity 0 to 1, scale 0 to 4; target 0 is a red cell and a blue cell, target 1 is a green cell and a yellow cell; one segment from 0 s for 2 s that weights target 0 by the constant 1 and target 1 by the input time), with time_seconds 0.5. The AI runs: cargo run --release --quiet --manifest-path trillion-workshop/tools/pointillist-film/Cargo.toml --target-dir /tmp/pointillist-film-build --example encode_frame_request -- request.json frame.pfcf
worked_examples.hands_back: Nothing on standard output and exit 0; frame.pfcf is 54 bytes (22 header bytes and 16 for each of the 2 cells): it starts with the text PFCF, then columns 2, rows 1, the time 0.5 and the cell count 2; running it again gives the same 54 bytes. With the grid set to 99 columns it prints "Error: GridAxisExceedsLimit { axis: \"columns\", value: 99, max: 8 }", exits 1 and writes nothing.
